event.title: Tanker Collides with River Cruise Ship in New Orleans, All Passengers Rescued
event.canonical_title: Tanker Collides with River Cruise Ship in New Orleans, All Passengers Rescued
event.summary: A tanker collided with a river cruise ship docked in New Orleans, causing the vessel to capsize. Approximately 130 people were on board, and all passengers and crew were accounted for after a large rescue operation. More than 30 individuals were hospitalized due to injuries sustained during the incident.

timeline.title: All Rescued After Tanker Collision with Cruise Ship on Mississippi River
timeline.summary: A tanker collided with a luxury paddle wheeler docked in New Orleans, causing the cruise vessel to roll over and sink. Fortunately, all passengers were rescued without fatalities, leading to the incident being referred to as a 'miracle on the Mississippi.' In response, New Orleans port officials have filed a lawsuit seeking at least $1 million in damages and requesting control of the tanker involved in the crash.
key_facts: Tanker collided with a luxury paddle wheeler in New Orleans.
The cruise vessel rolled over and sank, but all passengers were rescued.
New Orleans port officials filed a lawsuit for at least $1 million in damages.

event_overview.title: About Mississippi River Incident
event_overview.subject: Mississippi River Incident
event_overview.summary: The Mississippi River Incident is the November 13, 2026 marine casualty in which the tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck American Cruise Lines’ docked paddlewheeler American Heritage at the Port of New Orleans. The passenger vessel took on water and capsized, prompting a multiagency rescue; American Cruise Lines said all passengers and crew were safely accounted for, while the cause remained under investigation.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The allision occurred around 12:30 p.m. local time on November 13, 2026, on the Mississippi River beside the Port of New Orleans administration building; the American Heritage had been docked and was beginning passenger disembarkation.

facts.label: Vessels involved
facts.value: The moving vessel was the tanker Atlantic Asphalt; the stationary passenger vessel was American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage, a Mississippi River paddlewheeler.

facts.label: Passenger vessel profile
facts.value: American Cruise Lines lists the American Heritage as a 2015-built paddlewheeler with a 150-guest capacity, operating on the Mississippi River.

facts.label: Rescue outcome
facts.value: American Cruise Lines reported on November 14 that all passengers and crew had been evacuated and were safe and accounted for.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The National Transportation Safety Board deployed investigators; as of November 14, its expected timetable was a preliminary report within about 30 days and a final report, including probable cause findings, in roughly 18 to 24 months.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the initial November 14-15 rescue and accounting developments, not the full salvage operation, litigation, or the eventual official findings on cause and responsibility.
